info.title: General
info.html:
• Ethereal bonus reduced from 50% to 25% (most exceptional/elite weapons rebalanced so that eth stats remain the same)
  • Ethereal items no longer have half durability
  • Strength and Dexterity requirements of ethereal items are reduced by 10 each
  • Throwing weapons (including potions) and arrows/bolts have unlimited quantity
  • All claws can now have pointmods (staffmods) - previously, claws couldn't if they had a qlvl below 40: all normal claws, Quhab, Wrist Spike, Fascia
  • Clubs can now have Druid pointmods
  • Daggers can now have pointmods for dagger-related skills (Poison Strike and most martial arts skills)
  • Quivers can now be Magic, Rare, and Unique
  • Quivers can now roll 1-2 sockets
  • Quivers now have Normal, Exceptional, and Elite versions
  • Quivers now have automods

info.title: Automods
info.html:
Modifiers that automatically appear on all regular/magic/rare/crafted versions of items, and often unique/set versions too

Weapons

  • Melee weapons now have Melee Attacks Deal Splash Damage (except wands)
  • Staves now have 10%/30%/50% Faster Cast Rate (normal/exceptional/elite)
  • Daggers now have 20% Deadly Strike
  • Throwing Knives have 15% Critical Strike Multiplier

Quivers

  • Arrows now have +2/+10/+18 to Maximum Damage (normal/exceptional/elite)
  • Bolts now have -2%/-4%/-6% to Enemy Physical Resistance (normal/exceptional/elite)

Armor

  • Removed hidden -5%/-10% movespeed penalty from medium/heavy chests and shields
  • Paladin shields have reduced ranges for "All Resistances" automod
    • Rainbow reduced from +[8-15] to +[5-10]
    • Scintillating reduced from +[16-30] to +[10-15]
    • Prismatic reduced from +[25-35] to +[15-20]
    • Chromatic reduced from +[36-45] to +[20-30]
  • Spiked Shield, Barbed Shield, and Blade Barrier have Attackers take [2-4]/[16-20]/[80-100] Damage
  • Bone Shield, Grim Shield, and Troll Nest have Magic Damage Reduced by [2-4]/[4-6]/[6-8]

info.title: Damage
info.html:
Damage Bonus from Strength/Dexterity

  • Polearms, Non-Class Spears, & One-Handed Swords now gain bonus damage equal to 75% str & 75% dex instead of 100% str. This doesn't include Two-Handed swords that are wielded one-handed.
  • Staves & Two-Handed Axes/Swords now gain bonus damage equal to 110% str instead of 100% str (same as Hammers)
  • Bows/Crossbows now gain bonus damage equal to 50% dex instead of 100% dex
  • Boots now gain bonus damage equal to 80% str instead of 120% str and kicks also benefit roughly twice as much from dexterity (now dex/3 - dex/2, was dex/6 - dex/5)

For example: A Bow gets +5% Enhanced Damage if you get +10 to Dexterity.

Base Damage

  • Normal weapon damage increased by ~4% on average
  • Exceptional weapon damage increased by ~42% on average to be closer to elite weapons and counteract the ethereal bonus being changed from 1.5x to 1.25x
  • Elite weapon damage increased by ~24% on average to counteract the ethereal bonus being changed from 1.5x to 1.25x, along with a few relatively minor adjustments for specific bases
  • Kick damage of boots adjusted
  • In Season 11 bow base damage was increased by 20% (30% for Matriarchal). Lesser basses haven't yet been updated to reflect this, only elite. Percentage increase from LoD to S11 also hasn't been updated.

For weapons with two damage ranges, their 1-hand melee damage is listed second. Wands and Orbs are not listed here since they aren't attacked with (and their damage is unchanged)

info.title: Speed
info.html:
• Amazon spear weapon speed modifiers improved by 10

Negative values mean the weapon attacks faster. Wands and Orbs are not listed here since they aren't attacked with (and their speed is unchanged)

info.title: Melee Range
info.html:
• Daggers and throwing knives/axes increased to 1 range
  • All other melee weapons increased to 2 range
  • Javelins and two-handed melee weapons increased to 3 range (except 1x3 staves)
  • Spears and 2x4 sized axes/maces increased to 4 range

Bows, Crossbows, Wands, and Orbs are not listed here because they aren't attacked with in melee combat (and their melee range is zero)

info.title: Defense & Required Strength
info.html:
• Defense for chests adjusted - those with higher strength requirements will generally have more defense (tier and quality level were also considered)
  • Defense for Aegis and Ward shields increased
  • Strength requirement of Shadow Plate reduced from 230 to 220

info.html:
Paladins get +30% base block chance, Amazons/Assassins/Barbarians get +25% base block chance, and Druids/Necromancers/Sorceresses get +20% base block chance

  • Aegis base block chance increased from 24% to 46%
  • Ward base block chance increased from 24% to 32%
  • Royal Shield base block chance reduced from 25% to 23%
  • Sacred Targe base block chance reduced from 30% to 25%
  • Sacred Rondache base block chance reduced from 28% to 27%
  • Kurast Shield base block chance increased from 25% to 29%
  • Zakarum Shield base block chance increased from 22% to 31%
  • Vortex Shield base block chance increased from 19% to 32%

info.title: Sockets
info.html:
Weapons

  • Maximum sockets increased by 1 for several exceptional/elite weapons
    • 1-socket daggers (Poignard, Bone Knife, Rondel, Mithril Point) can now get 2 sockets
    • 2-socket 1x3 weapons that can now get 3 sockets:
      • Axes (Hatchet, Tomahawk)
      • Maces (Cudgel, Truncheon, Flanged Mace, Reinforced Mace)
      • Swords (Gladius, Falcata, Cutlass, Ataghan, Shamshir, Elegant Blade, Tulwar, Hydra Edge)
      • Staves (Jo Staff, Walking Stick)
      • Scepters (Rune Scepter, Mighty Scepter)
      • Claws (Wrist Spike, Fascia, War Fist, Hand Scythe, Battle Cestus)
    • 3-socket two-handed weapons that can now get 4 sockets:
      • Polearms (Lochaber Axe, Ogre Axe)
      • Spears (War Spear)
      • Staves (Stalagmite)
      • Bows (Edge Bow, Spider Bow)
      • Crossbows (Arbalest, Pellet Bow)
    • 3-socket two-handed weapons that can now get 6 sockets:
      • Spears (Hyperion Spear)
    • 4-socket two-handed axes (Military Axe, Feral Axe) can now get 5 sockets
    • 5-socket Shadow Bow can now get 6 sockets
  • Throwing weapons can now get sockets

Another way to look at most of the weapon socket changes:

  • All exceptional/elite 1x2 weapons can now get 2 sockets except for Burnt Wand
  • All exceptional/elite 1x3 weapons can now get 3 sockets except for a dagger line (Stiletto, Legend Spike)
  • All exceptional/elite two-handed weapons (1x4 or larger) can now get 4 sockets except for a sword line (Espandon, Legend Sword), a spear line (War Spear), and a staff line (Quarterstaff)

Weapons with multiple values such as 3/4/6 have different maximum sockets depending on their ilvl (1-25/26-40/41+) and the socket values are colored orange if the item's quality level is higher than the ilvl range, signifying they won't drop at those ilvls.


Armor

  • Maximum sockets for exceptional/elite Necromancer shields increased from 2 to 3
  • Maximum sockets for the following shields increased from 2 to 3: Spiked Shield, Barbed Shield, Grim Shield

Armor with multiple values such as 3/4/4 have different maximum sockets depending on their ilvl (1-25/26-40/41+) and the socket values are colored orange if the item's quality level is higher than the ilvl range, signifying they won't drop at those ilvls. Gloves, boots, and belts are not listed here because they cannot get sockets.

info.title: Durability
info.html:
• Durability for all weapons has been doubled
  • Some elite weapons have even more durability:
    • +20 durability for some swords (Falcata, Ataghan, Elegant Blade, Hydra Edge, Conquest Sword)
    • +20 durability for Bone Knife
    • +20 durability for some axes (Decapitator, Champion Axe, Glorious Axe)
    • +50% durability for other axes (Tomahawk, Small Crescent, Ettin Axe, War Spike, Berserker Axe, Feral Axe, Silver-edged Axe)
    • +50% durability for spears (Hyperion Spear, Stygian Pike, Mancatcher, Ghost Spear, War Pike)
    • +50% durability for staves (Walking Stick, Stalagmite, Elder Staff, Shillelagh, Archon Staff), additional +50% for Walking Stick

Missile Weapons, Throwing Weapons, Wands, and Orbs are not listed because they either don't have durability or are not attacked with so won't lose durability.

info.title: Runes
info.html:
All runes are now stackable. Runes can be switched between their stacked and unstacked forms with shortcuts, and can only be placed in items when in their unstacked form.

For rune effects that have been changed, changes are shown in blue with the original effects shown in gray.

The term "high rune" refers to any rune that cannot drop from the Hellforge quest, which is Vex or higher. It is not to be confused with the troublesomely-named "HR" unit of currency, which can be used with any sufficiently-valuable item rather than just high runes.

High runes typically form the core of market trading currencies due to their rarity and general usefulness, while upper "mid runes" (Lem through Gul) are close enough in value to be traded in a similar fashion, especially during the beginning of each ladder season. Below Lem, rune values are too low for individual runes to be practically referred to in terms of HRs, and are traded more often in bulk rather than as individual tokens of currency. Beyond runes, few items are used as ubiquitously as currency, with the most notable exception being Worldstone Shards.

info.title: Gems
info.html:
Flawless and Perfect gems are now stackable. Flawless gems now begin dropping in Act 4 Normal, and Perfect gems can now drop in Hell.

Gem effects have not been changed from vanilla D2, but are included here for convenience.

sections.title: General
sections.html:
• Mercenaries inherit the player's Magic and Gold Find when they kill enemies (e.g. if the player has 200% MF and the merc has 100% MF, the merc's total MF will be 300%)
  • Mercenaries have improved AI
  • New mercenaries:
    • One additional version of Act 1 mercenaries
    • New Act 4 mercenaries (two versions) which are robed mages of the Horadrim
    • One additional version of Act 5 mercenaries (different than D2R's dual-wield Barbarian)
  • Mercenaries can no longer proc summon skills (this prevents crashes)

sections.title: Equipment
sections.html:
• All mercenaries can equip helms, chests, gloves, boots, & belts.
  • Act 1 mercenaries (Rogue Scouts) can equip bows (including Amazon bows), crossbows, & quivers.
  • Act 2 mercenaries (Desert Guards) can equip polearms, spears, & javelins.
  • Act 3 mercenaries (Iron Wolves) can equip shields, Paladin shields, 1-handed swords, wands, scepters, tipped maces (not clubs/hammers), & Sorceress orbs.
  • Act 4 mercenaries (Ascendants) can equip staves.
  • Act 5 mercenaries (Barbarians) can equip swords, axes, tipped maces/hammers (all maces except clubs), & Barbarian helms.
  • Old mercenaries drop their equipped items when a new one is hired.
  • Ethereal items do not lose durability when mercenaries use them.
  • Mercenaries can get set bonuses when equipping multiple set items.
  • When Desert Guards or Barbarian mercenaries use 1-handed weapons, their weapon damage is doubled - this makes 1-handed and 2-handed weapons more comparable.
  • Barbarian mercenaries can't equip two 1-handed weapons.

sections.title: Skill Information
sections.html: • For detailed information on Mercenary Skills, see: Mercenary Skills.

sections.title: Aura Changes
sections.html: Auras available on each Mercenary have been revised and expanded.

sections.title: Skill Changes
sections.html:
• Act 1 mercenaries (Rogue Scouts) now use the following skills:
    • Fire: No longer uses Inner Sight
    • Cold: No longer uses Inner Sight
    • Physical (new type): Magic Arrow, Strafe, & Slow Movement.
  • Act 3 mercenaries (Iron Wolves) now have passive mastery skills which grant elemental bonuses and Life after each Kill, and they use the following skills:
    • Fire: Meteor instead of Fire Bolt
    • Cold: Blizzard instead of Glacial Spike & Chilling Armor
    • Lightning: No longer uses Charged Bolt
  • Act 5 mercenaries (Barbarians) now use the following skills:
    • Combat: Concentrate instead of Stun.
    • Warcries: Whirlwind, Battle Cry and Battle Orders instead of Bash & Stun.
    • Dual-Wielding Frenzy/Taunt Act 5 Mercenary from Diablo 2: Resurrected is not implemented into Project Diablo 2.
  • Mercenaries use Merc-specific versions of some skills which are balanced separately from player skills.

sections.title: Stats
sections.html:
• Mercenaries have the same stats regardless of which difficulty they're hired from
  • Mercenary stats have been adjusted:
    • Stat scaling has been improved to be more consistent throughout the game
    • Desert Guards and Barbarian mercenaries now gain slightly less damage per level


Notes:

  • The above Attack Rating values do not take into account the extra AR given from dex
  • Attack Rating always shows up on the advanced character stats page as 0. This is likely just an issue with the advanced stats page (all other stats show up correctly)
  • Mercenaries hired from different difficulties can have different stats at lower levels, as described in the example below. Any merc that's level 80 or above will have the same stats regardless of which difficulty they were hired in.
Example Stat Differences

The game uses several level "thresholds" to determine merc stats and ensure they're the same between difficulties. Normal has 3 of these thresholds, Nightmare has 2, and Hell has 1 (Normal threshold #3 == Nightmare threshold #2 == Hell threshold #1)

This is mostly just an issue in instances where a low level character is in a higher difficulty than expected.

We'll use an Act 1 Rogue as an example as to how you could get stats that differ from the above tables. In NM the Rogue's level thresholds are 36 & 67, and in hell the threshold is 67. Let's hire a level 67 Rogue and look at some of their stats:

NM: HP: 900 Def: 744 Resist: 121
Hell: HP: 900 Def: 744 Resist: 121

The above stats all match, so in this case it does not matter which difficulty you hire your Rogue in. But what happens if we hire a level 66 Rogue?

NM: HP: 882 Def: 729 Resist: 118
Hell: HP: 870 Def: 722 Resist: 120

In this case sometimes the Hell Rogue ends up with slightly worse stats and sometimes slightly better. So what about a level 36 Rogue?

NM: HP: 342 Def: 279 Resist: 66
Hell: HP: 40 Def: 18 Resist: 80

This is a pretty drastic difference. However, as soon as the Rogue levels up to 67 then the stats will match again - regardless of which difficulty they were hired in.

sections.title: Other Info
sections.html:
• Act 1 mercenaries (Rogue Scouts) now have a baseline 66% pierce chance.
  • Open Wounds now deals ¼ damage to mercenaries and pets, and can be further reduced by Physical Damage Reduction.
  • Mercenaries only have Strength and Dexterity, so items with Vitality or Energy will have no effect. They do have life (of course) but do not have mana - they ignore mana costs when using their skills.
  • Mercenaries use the same breakpoints for all weapon types. For example, Rogue Scouts will attack at the same speed with bows and crossbows (assuming they have the same WSM and IAS) whereas characters usually attack much slower with crossbows.
  • Iron Wolves don't have a blocking animation, so they can't block even while wearing a shield.
  • Barbarian mercenaries don't have a hit recovery animation, so cannot be put into hit recovery or be knocked back.

See PD2's data files [1] for updated info when game changes are made. General mercenary info is in Hireling.txt and merc-specific skills are alongside other skills in Skills.txt. The files are best viewed in table format since they are tab-delineated, so they should be opened with Microsoft Excel (or similar programs) or their text should be copy/pasted into a spreadsheet.

If the files in these locations are not up to date, you can extract them yourself from pd2data.mpq (found in Diablo II/ProjectD2) using an MPQ editor and D2 listfile - the text files will be in /data/global/excel.

sections.title: Skill Info
sections.html:
• Mercenaries have "Hard Levels" in their Skills, so they will gain those effects.
  • Mercenaries can also get synergies on their Skills, in the same way players do.
    • This applies to both their "natural" Skills and Skills from items they equip, if the Skill granting the synergy is the exact skill (i.e., not a Mercenary-only skill).
    • See below for synergies Mercenaries get from their "natural" Skills.
    • Mercenary Skills will also grant synergies to Skills from items. For example, an Act 2 Offensive mercenary wearing Doom will grant (up to) +198% Cold Damage on the Holy Freeze from his (up to) Hard Level 18 Blessed Aim.
    • Since Mercenaries get 'Hard' levels past 20, unlike players, synergy bonuses can be even higher than players get.
  • Skills and Auras have minimum level requirements, so mercenaries won't be able to use some skills at lower levels.
  • Mercenaries will benefit from the following +Skill bonuses:
    • +X to All Skills
    • +X to non-class Fire/Cold/Lightning/Magic Skills (as applicable to a skill)
    • +X to specific Skills if they use the Skill (e.g. a Barbarian helmet with +3 to Bash for an Act 5 Combat Mercenary, or a +3 Prayer Scepter for an Act 3 Cold Mercenary). The (Class Only) tag does not apply as long as the skill is an exact match.
      • Specific skill bonuses will only work if the skill is the exact same skill Players use (i.e., not a Mercenary-only skill).
  • Mercenaries will not benefit from:
    • +X to Class Skills (not even Act 5 Barbarians)
    • +X to Class Skill Trees (e.g. +X to Offensive Auras or +X to Combat Skills)
  • Each time mercenaries attack or use a skill, they choose which skill to use at random based on set probabilities.
    • For more information see Below: (Act 1, Act 2, Act 3, Act 4, Act 5)
    • Passive Skills and Auras are always active, and thus are not listed.

sections.title: Auras
sections.html:
• Most Mercenaries from all acts now have auras, rather than just Act 2 mercenaries.
Mercenary Subtype Aura
Act 1 (Rogue) Fire Vigor
Act 1 (Rogue) Cold Meditation
Act 1 (Rogue) Physical None (Slow Movement)
Act 2 (Desert Guard) Defensive Defiance
Act 2 (Desert Guard) Offensive Blessed Aim
Act 2 (Desert Guard) Combat Thorns
Act 3 (Iron Wolf) Fire Cleansing
Act 3 (Iron Wolf) Cold Prayer
Act 3 (Iron Wolf) Lightning Holy Shock (& Static Field)
Act 4 (Ascendant) Dark None (Amplify Damage)
Act 4 (Ascendant) Light Sanctuary
Act 5 (Barbarian) Combat Might
Act 5 (Barbarian) Warcries None (Battle Orders & Battle Cry)
  • Mercenary Auras are always active as long as the level requirement has been met.
    • The level requirement for each Mercenary Aura is the same as for the corresponding Paladin Skill.
  • The difficulty in which a Mercenary is hired no longer affects the Aura the Mercenary has.
  • Mercenaries' native Auras and Auras granted from their items interact the same way as they do on players, meaning mercenaries can have multiple auras from skills and items, but an Aura granted by an item will not stack with an identical native Aura.
    • For example, an Act 1 Fire Mercenary's Vigor Aura will not benefit from wearing Harmony - the skill Aura will override the item Aura.
